Anna —

Appreciate the clear ask and the redline. Quick read-through: we agree with harmonizing the terms and can propose a short definitions section in Annex B. A couple of operational notes up front so the legal language maps cleanly to what we actually do:

- "Erase" should be reserved for an operator-initiated, customer-requested full data removal (triggered by API/portal request or termination).
- "Purge" we use internally to mean irreversible deletion from primary stores; however backups/snapshots may be marked for purge but only physically removed on the scheduled snapshot sweep.
- "Tombstone" will be our transient marker state; we can add explicit timestamps (marked_at / effective_delete_date) to the clause so audit can correlate logs.

I'll attach a one-page diagram (erase-flow-diagram.png) and a short suggested paragraph we can slot into Annex B. Can your side confirm whether "onshore backup" must be explicitly listed as a separate category from "local copy" for the contract, or if a defined term like "Onshore Replicas (as defined below)" is acceptable?

Target: we can produce a harmonized redline (tracked) by Monday EOD. If that works, we'll prep a DocuSign-ready annex.

Looping in a few technical clarifications for the redline (internal only):

- Snapshots: We create point-in-time FS snapshots for rapid restore. These are logically "backups" but are stored in the same region as primary; their retention is 14 days by default for prod, configurable to 90d on Dedicated accounts. For DPA language, suggest we say: "Temporary snapshots (retention <= 90 days) are excluded from immediate final deletion and subject to scheduled purge flows unless an expedited erasure request is initiated."

- Onshore backup vs local copy: Operationally, "Local copy" = data stored in the customer's selected region; "Onshore backup" = copies replicated to the customer's legal jurisdiction (e.g., EU) specifically for compliance. Proposed clause: "Onshore Replicas — copies of Customer Data stored within the Customer's designated jurisdiction and subject to the same retention and erasure controls as Primary Data."

- Evidence manifest: We can provide a machine-readable manifest showing: object id, tombstone timestamp, purge-scheduled timestamp, and final-delete-confirmation. Suggest limiting manifest retention to 12 months post-final-delete for audit purposes.

Suggested insertion for Annex B (redline plain text):
"For clarity, the following terms shall have the meanings set forth below: (i) 'Tombstone' — a metadata marker indicating the initiation of an erasure workflow; (ii) 'Purge' — the process by which data becomes unrecoverable from production storage; (iii) 'Final Delete' — irreversible removal from backup media as scheduled by the purge sweep. Evidence manifests will be produced upon completion of Final Delete and retained for a maximum of twelve (12) months unless otherwise required by law."

I'll add this text to the tracked redline and push to the Drive link Logan mentioned.
